title: Map PNG Export: Map Images for Documents
description: Use Map PNG Export to prepare and capture a map view as a PNG image for documents, slides and reports — framed right, credited properly. Free.
summary_sentence: For example, a consultant frames the project site once, exports the PNG, and the same clean map image appears in the proposal, the appendix and the council presentation.
quick_answer: Map PNG Export helps you prepare a map view and capture it as a PNG image for documents, presentations and reports. Frame the view — centre, zoom, layers — and export an image that drops into Word, slides or a PDF cleanly.

popular_table.title: Framing checklist before you export
popular_table.intro: Thirty seconds here saves the re-export round trip.
rows: The subject should sit with room for captions and arrows
Export at the zoom you will display — enlarging later pixelates
Turn off layers the document does not discuss
Base-map credit (© OpenStreetMap contributors) should survive into the document
popular_table.note: A PNG is a picture of a map, not map data: it cannot be re-measured or restyled later. Keep the live view's link or the GeoJSON alongside the image in your project file.

faq: What size is the exported image?

The export captures the prepared view at screen-class resolution suitable for documents and slides. For wall-size printing, frame the widest view offered and check the result at 100% before committing paper.
Can I export a map I annotated?
Yes — build the annotated view first (pins, labels, legend) in the maker tools, then export the composed view so the image carries your layer, not just the basemap.
Is the PNG free to publish?

The tool is free; the basemap inside the picture carries its own licence. OpenStreetMap data asks for a visible credit (© OpenStreetMap contributors) — keep the attribution line in your document and you are on solid ground.
Why not just take a screenshot?
You can — and for quick chats it is fine. The export path exists to frame deliberately, capture cleanly at a known size and avoid browser chrome, cursors and half-loaded tiles in the deliverable.
Can I get a vector (SVG) instead?
This tool's promise is PNG for documents. Vector outlines live in the Blank Map family for country and state shapes; street-level vector export is GIS territory.
The text looks small in my document.
Text size is fixed by the basemap at capture zoom. Export at a closer zoom, or present the map larger — shrinking a wide-area export into a narrow column makes every label microscopic.
Can I export in satellite view?
If the view you prepare is the satellite basemap, the export captures that view. Same framing rules apply — and satellite imagery carries its provider's credit line too.
Does the export include a scale bar?
For print-critical scale, prepare the view with the Printable Map with Scale Context tool so the scale is designed for paper rather than inherited from the screen.
